summary: Codex's history is 491 days and 9545 commits in which the project changed shape three times. It began in April 2025 as an open-source TypeScript CLI with a 95-author community burst, imported a parallel Rust implementation eight days later, and deleted the TypeScript code by August 2025. From August 2025 to March 2026 it became a pure Rust workspace where the TUI was the product and the app-server JSON-RPC API was born (2025-09-30); a forked tui2 experiment was abandoned after six weeks, and in March 2026 a second rewrite succeeded in twelve days, moving the TUI on top of the app-server and deleting the legacy TUI. Since April 2026, the busiest month (1060 commits), the work is decomposing the core into crates and building an extension and plugin platform (ext/, core-plugins, codex-mcp, features, state), all broad-based rather than single-owner. Velocity is a high plateau (2818 commits in the last 90 days versus 2856 before) with a growing, now 95% in-house team of about 195 active authors; ownership of the core moved from the original author to a contributor who arrived in September 2025. Attention items are modest: the core still takes 46% of recent commits despite the extraction programme, the external-agent-migration crate is effectively single-owner, and the deprecated mcp-server crate still ships.

findings.title: Era 1 (2025-04 to 2025-08): the TypeScript CLI, with a Rust rewrite growing beside it
findings.description: From the first commit on 2025-04-16 to early August 2025 the project was an **open-source TypeScript CLI** under `codex-cli/`, which took 60% of the 256 commits of April 2025 from 95 different authors. Eight days after the initial commit, on 2025-04-24, the **Rust implementation was imported** into `codex-rs/` in a single 71-file, 14099-line commit, and from May on `codex-rs/core` and `codex-rs/tui` already dominated the monthly activity. The era is a community burst followed by a lull: 157 commits in May, 44 in June with only 5 authors, 128 in July. The Rust CLI was declared the released product in July 2025 (`docs: update documentation to reflect Rust CLI release`). The era left behind the `codex-cli/` npm wrapper, the `codex-rs/execpolicy` and `mcp-types` crates, and the sandboxing work (Landlock/seccomp) that still frames the product.

findings.title: Era 2 (2025-08 to 2025-11): one Rust codebase, the TUI as the product, the app-server born
findings.description: After the **TypeScript code was deleted** on 2025-08-09 (216 files, 35960 lines removed), the repository became a pure Rust workspace and activity jumped from 128 commits in July to 426 in August 2025. The TUI was the center of the product: `codex-rs/tui` had its highest share ever in August (47% of commits) with the markdown-streaming work (landed, reverted, re-landed) and the animation frames of September. The `codex-rs/protocol` crate appears in 2025-08 and the **`codex app-server` split from `codex mcp`** on 2025-09-30 opened the JSON-RPC API that everything later builds on. October brought the first large refactors by the contributor who would become the top committer (`refactor tool handling`, `unify config crates`) and the Windows sandbox alpha. The era closed with the `execpolicy2` cutover and the first `app-server-protocol` crate in November.

findings.title: Era 3 (2025-12 to 2026-03): the app-server becomes the platform and the TUI is rebuilt on it
findings.description: From December 2025 activity accelerated month over month (427, 641, 887, 835 commits) and the **app-server became the architectural center**: its share of commits rose from 16% to 24% while `codex-rs/core` peaked at 63% in March 2026. Two frontend experiments define the era, told in detail in the lifecycle group: the `tui2` copy-and-improve experiment (December to January, retired) and the **`tui_app_server` rewrite** that moved the TUI on top of the app-server and replaced the legacy TUI within twelve days in March 2026. In parallel the core started to be decomposed (`codex-config` extracted in February, `codex-command` split out) and the protocol got a vendored JSON schema fixture tree of 91513 lines. The era closed with the TUI rename on 2026-03-28, after which every UI is an app-server client.

findings.title: Era 4 (2026-04 to now): peak volume, core decomposition and an extension ecosystem
findings.description: April 2026 was the **busiest month ever** (1060 commits, 89 authors) and the following four months stayed between 779 and 938 commits with 87 to 119 authors each. The dominant theme is restructuring what the previous era piled into the core: `codex.rs` moved under `session/` and was split, the models manager was extracted, the app-server request processors and transport were split into crates, and shared HTTP transport went to `codex-http-client`. New areas were born in quick succession: `codex-rs/core-plugins` (2026-04), `codex-rs/codex-mcp` (2026-04), `codex-rs/features` and `codex-rs/tools` (2026-03), and above all **`codex-rs/ext/`** (2026-05), a directory of first-party extensions (skills, guardian-v2, memories, mcp, git-attribution) behind an `extension-api`. The recent commit stream is about plugins, Guardian approval routing, exec-server tracing and MCP hardening, which is where the trajectory points.

findings.title: Growth curve: 91% of all commits landed in the last twelve months, peaking in April 2026
findings.description: The history spans 491 days (2025-04-16 to 2026-08-20) with **9545 commits by 581 authors**, but the curve is far from flat. Lines added per month grew from 41k in April 2025 to 731k in March 2026 (the TUI rewrite month, which also removed 516k) and 271k in August 2026. findings.title: Team over time: from a 95-author open-source burst to a 100+ engineer in-house team
findings.description: The contributor base changed character twice. April 2025 had **95 authors in one month**, most of them one-off external contributors to the TypeScript CLI; by June 2025 only 5 authors were active. From August 2025 the team grew steadily: 38, 43, 47, 70 authors per month in late 2025 and 87 to 119 per month in 2026, with **195 distinct authors in the last 90 days** (up from 156 in the previous 90). Of 581 authors all-time, 329 have a single commit and 421 have three or fewer, so the effective team is far smaller than the headline. The share of commits from `@openai.com` addresses rose from 68% (Apr to Jul 2025) to 81% (Aug to Dec 2025) to 95% in 2026: the project is now developed almost entirely in-house, with external contributions marginal.

findings.title: Rewrite 2 (abandoned): the tui2 copy-and-improve experiment lived six weeks
findings.description: On 2025-12-10 the TUI crate was **copied wholesale into `codex-rs/tui2`** (742 files, 53559 lines) behind a feature flag, kept in sync with dual-run glue, and given a burst of transcript-selection, scrolling and rendering work (28 `tui2` commits in December and January, 17% of January's commits). On 2026-01-22 the experiment was **retired in a single commit removing 808 files and 82801 lines**. `codex-rs/tui2` no longer exists. The lesson the history records is that a forked copy of a 1500-file crate diverged too fast to keep in sync; the next TUI rewrite (below) used a different strategy and succeeded.

findings.title: Rewrite 3 (completed in 12 days): the TUI was moved on top of the app-server and the legacy TUI removed
findings.description: On 2026-03-16 a **parallel `tui_app_server` crate** (1109 files, 134243 lines) landed that drove the TUI through the app-server JSON-RPC API instead of calling `codex-core` directly. Over the next eleven days a stream of `tui_app_server` fix commits removed the remaining core events and legacy auth handling, the feature was enabled by default, and on 2026-03-27 the **legacy TUI was removed** (856 files, 130858 lines). On 2026-03-28 the crate was renamed back to `tui` (1968 files touched). This is the turning point that made 'every UI is an app-server client' true; the 1124 deleted files under `tui_app_server` in the lifecycle numbers are this rename, not lost work. Today `codex-rs/tui` depends on `codex-app-server-client`, and no `tui_app_server` directory remains.

findings.title: Velocity: a high plateau, not acceleration, with a broadening team
findings.description: The 90-day comparison is flat: **2818 commits in the last 90 days versus 2856 in the previous 90**, after the April 2026 peak of 1060 commits in a month. Monthly volume has settled between 779 and 938 since May. Authors are still growing (195 active in 90 days versus 156), so the plateau is not a shrinking team but a steady one producing at the same rate with more hands, which typically means more reviewers and smaller commits. The project is neither accelerating nor decelerating; it is running at the highest sustained rate in its history.

findings.title: Work mix now: restructuring and hardening replace bug-fixing, and the messages stopped saying 'fix'
findings.description: The script's commit-theme classifier shows `fix` falling from 23% of commits in the older half of the last year to 12% in the recent half, `feature` from 30% to 25%, `refactor` rising from 4% to 6%, `security` from 1.6% to 3.6%, `test` from 1.9% to 4.4%, and `other` rising from 25% to 42%. Reading the recent messages, the `other` growth is largely a **house style change**: 2026 commit titles are imperative verbs without conventional prefixes (`Harden`, `Restrict`, `Isolate`, `Trace`, `Consolidate`), so the classifier under-counts fixes and refactors. Reading them, the recent quarter is dominated by **hardening and restructuring**: plugin isolation, Guardian approval routing, exec-server tracing, MCP process cleanup, and crate extractions, with feature work concentrated in extensions and plugins. Feature work has not stopped, so this is a healthy maturing mix rather than a fixes-only drift.

findings.title: Direction: from a terminal agent to an extensible agent platform, with the risks that implies
findings.description: The facts above point one way. Activity moved from the TUI to the app-server and core; the last quarter's births are all platform machinery (`ext/`, `core-plugins`, `codex-mcp`, `features`, `state`); the top contributor's recent work is the extension registry and Guardian; and the README now offers the CLI, an IDE integration, a desktop app and a cloud agent as peers. Codex is **turning into an agent platform** whose terminal UI is one client. The trajectory implies three risks already visible in the history: the core keeps absorbing half of all commits while being decomposed (lifecycle), one young crate is single-owner (people), and a deprecated crate still ships (lifecycle). None is acute today; the sustained 90-day velocity and broad ownership of the emerging areas are the strongest positive signals.
